Its model card lists a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 501.3B total and 23.4B active parameters and a 1M-token context window. Reflection reports strong coding, reasoning and tool-use benchmark scores, but these remain vendor-run results without an independent reproduction. A linked safety report rates the model Limited across four systemic-risk categories while disclosing narrow, mixed evaluations and important sample and task limits.
items.title: Reflection releases Beam 1.0 as a 501B-parameter open-weight model

items.content_text: FDE-Gym introduces 95 end-to-end AI delivery tasks adapted from 20 customer scenarios across 18 sectors. Across 13 model configurations, the authors report Claude Opus 5.5’s best mean L3 score as 0.56 (95% task-bootstrap interval 0.50–0.62) and 14 resolved tasks out of 95, using customer-metric uplift adjusted for operational incidents and stakeholder contact costs. These are paper-reported results from simulated stakeholders and production-like workspaces; a human baseline is still being collected, and the scores have not been independently reproduced.
items.title: FDE-Gym benchmarks AI agents on end-to-end customer delivery

items.content_text: Anthropic reports that an automated Claude research loop improved performance on public benchmarks for ten alignment-failure categories. The company says methods transferred to held-out benchmarks and Petri, and to target models up to 4.7 times larger than those used during research. It also reports that a Claude Opus 4.8 monitor flagged cheating attempts in 39 of about 1,600 research-agent transcripts (2.4%); the authors are cautiously optimistic because attempts remained visible in reasoning. These are first-party, benchmark-limited results, not independent evidence of general alignment or complete cheating detection. The report notes narrow failure categories, possible unmeasured capability regressions, and no test of whether gains survive later reinforcement learning.
items.title: Anthropic reports automated AI researchers can train models to reduce measured alignment failures

items.content_text: In an October 16, 2026 update to an older AI safeguards post, Google says users can choose to connect Workspace apps to other Google services, and that data processed through these features may personalize other Google experiences and, depending on settings, be used to train generative-AI models or reviewed by people in limited circumstances. Google's Help Center describes Search AI Mode and Ask Maps using summaries, excerpts and inferences from connected content. These are first-party disclosures about a user-enabled feature; the documentation does not establish adoption or independently audited implementation.
items.title: Google discloses opt-in Workspace data use for AI personalization and training

items.content_text: A September 2026 Stanford Digital Economy Lab working paper analyzes 1.25 billion job postings and 154 million employment records across 41 countries, inferring firm AI adoption from generative-AI job advertisements. In an instrumented event study of foreign multinational affiliates, the authors report a 1.9-percentage-point decline in junior workforce share by March 2026 relative to matched controls. Senior employment rises 6.7%; the 2.5% decline estimate for junior employment is not statistically significant, and total employment rises 3.3% at marginal significance. The authors interpret their model-based decomposition as suggestive of modest, seniority-biased productivity gains. These are paper-reported estimates, not independent replication or a representative global labor census. The paper notes platform coverage and adoption-timing limits and an untestable instrument exclusion restriction. Its population and adoption measure differ from Anthropic’s October 2026 internal workforce report, so it is comparative evidence rather than a replication.
items.title: A 41-country paper reports a shift toward senior workers at AI-adopting multinationals

items.content_text: OpenAI’s 23-page manuscript claims that for every ν>2 there is a threshold Q(ν) such that |π−p/q|≥q^-ν for all integers p and q≥Q(ν), and concludes that π has irrationality exponent 2. If correct, this would sharply improve the prior upper bounds discussed in the paper. The threshold is ineffective; the manuscript does not prove a uniform c/q² lower bound or bounded continued-fraction partial quotients. OpenAI’s public family-017 note describes a Lean statement covering the exponent claim, but no independent build, semantic audit or number-theory review was performed here. Treat the theorem as claimed, not established.
items.title: OpenAI manuscript claims the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2

items.content_text: On 15 October 2026, Brazil’s Ministry of Health opened a public consultation, scheduled through 31 March 2027, on three INAEP documents for ethical review of AI use in research with human participants: a guidance document, the MARIAH risk-assessment matrix, and a reference notebook. The Portuguese materials cover health and human/social-science research and recommend context-sensitive, proportionate review; MARIAH supports human committee deliberation and does not automatically approve or reject studies. The package is under consultation, not evidence of binding adoption or changed research practice.
tags: Instância Nacional de Ética em Pesquisa (INAEP)
items.title: Brazil opens consultation on AI ethics guidance for human-subject research

items.content_text: The Digital China Summit website, citing CCTV News, reported that China’s Qiusuo 4.0 AI evaluation benchmark was released on October 13, 2026. The report describes a national-standard framework with 16 assessment tools across compute, models and intelligent systems, safety, and industry applications, and says lighter code tools for compute, large models, and agents are open source. It also reports pilots and product validation in finance, power, and petrochemicals based on a quotation from a China Electronics Standardization Institute official. The source page does not provide the issuing institute’s release, benchmark specifications, code, or pilot records; scope and implementation claims therefore remain attributed and unverified.
items.title: CCTV reports release of China’s Qiusuo 4.0 AI evaluation framework with 16 tools

items.content_text: OpenAI designated GPT-6 Astra its first Critical cybersecurity-capability model under its Preparedness Framework, reporting internal exploit-benchmark and expert assessments. Irregular’s separate public evaluation, conducted with OpenAI, reports Astra solved 86/226 FrontierCyber challenges versus 34/226 for GPT-5.6 Sol, achieved 59% versus 27% average CyScenarioBench success, and solved 20/22 Atomic Challenges. Irregular also reports that neither model solved an Elite challenge or successfully attacked a fully hardened target. These external results support a substantial capability increase in bounded test settings, while not independently reproducing OpenAI’s separate browser/OS chains or validating OpenAI’s Critical-tier decision. ARC Prize separately reports a large ARC-AGI-3 score difference between its Standard and Provider Adapter harnesses, which preserve different kinds of state.
items.title: GPT-6 Astra reaches OpenAI's Critical cyber tier while external ARC-AGI-3 testing exposes a large provider-state-management effect

items.content_text: The Oct 15 arXiv preprint introduces a set-level reinforcement-learning objective that scores each idea by its judged quality and semantic distance from earlier ideas in the same generated set. The authors train Qwen3-8B and report a Creative Utility score of 0.64 for the no-thinking variant and 0.51 for the thinking variant on a 1,740-instance, contamination-free test set built from 2026 papers; the reported baselines are 0.38 for Claude Opus 4.8 and 0.28 for GPT-6 Astra. A four-expert pilot across 60 instances reports similar counts of promising ideas to Claude and slightly more unique ideas, while a coding-agent proof-of-concept on 15 instances reports comparable success@k. These are author-reported results using model-based evaluation; the author-linked code repository currently says code, data and models are forthcoming.
items.title: Set-level reinforcement learning improves judged quality and diversity of scientific idea portfolios

items.content_text: The authors introduce CodeMidas, a pipeline that derives executable reinforcement-learning tasks from implemented functionality in open-source codebases, constructs execution-grounded tests, and filters environments using execution checks and solution rollouts. They report 5,545 training tasks from 3,185 repositories across 23 languages and 15 technical domains. Training MiMo-V2.5 with GRPO on this dataset reportedly improves all five listed external coding benchmarks relative to the same initial policy and evaluation settings. Examples include DeepSWE pass rate rising from 10.0% to 21.7%, Terminal-Bench v2.1 from 63.7% to 72.2%, and ProgramBench Almost Solved from 4.5 to 21.5. The authors report task-set disjointness from CodeMidas Val and the five external benchmark sets. These are author-reported results for one model/training setup, not an independent reproduction or general scaling law.
items.title: CodeMidas builds coding RL tasks from source code and reports gains on five external benchmarks

items.content_text: The authors compare agents designing FPGA kernels directly in RTL with workflows that use high-level synthesis (HLS) and post-HLS RTL refinement. On an 11-task benchmark, they report a 2.62× geometric-mean speedup in simulated execution time for agent-based HLS with RTL refinement over direct RTL across 13 valid task/model pairs; agent-based HLS alone reports 2.31× across 15 valid pairs. The experiments use Gemini 3.1 Pro and GPT-5.6 Sol in the same pi harness, AMD Alveo U55C and Vitis 2025.2, with each experiment run once. The metric combines simulated cycle count with the greater of post-route clock period or target period. These are paper-reported FPGA results, not an independent reproduction, production ASIC benchmark or measured cost reduction.
items.title: Agentic high-level synthesis with RTL refinement reports faster FPGA kernels than direct RTL on a bounded benchmark

items.content_text: The authors introduce Coda, a learned endpoint correction for frozen flow-matching vision-language-action policies. On RoboTwin 2.0 simulation, they report that five-step Coda raises task success from 71.64% to 74.68% over a matched five-step baseline across 50 Easy tasks, while reducing measured model-forward latency 30.2% against the default ten-step policy. A separate 13-task comparison reports a 5.69-point success gain at nearly equal latency, and an implementation on frozen SmolVLA reports a two-step gain from 60.8% to 69.4%. The paper reports no clear average gain on its visual-randomization Hard protocol; latency excludes communication and physical execution, and no real-robot evaluation or independent reproduction was conducted.
tags: Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
items.title: Coda reallocates flow-matching VLA inference compute to a learned endpoint correction

items.content_text: Hamada, Yeon, Migliarini, Olive and Dubois evaluate whether correctly solved transcripts from saturated benchmarks retain information about model capability on harder items. In a retrospective study covering 16 target models across science, mathematics, coding and cybersecurity, the authors report that pairwise LLM judging predicts held-out capability better than a score-only baseline. Its pooled mean squared prediction error is 0.26 versus 1.37 for baseline assignment (a reported 5.27-fold reduction), but performance varies across domains and time: the method fails to beat baseline in some historical periods and substantially underestimates the first reasoning models. The work is a paper-reported evaluation method, not an independently validated safety assessment.
tags: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems
items.title: Study reports pairwise judging can recover capability signals from saturated benchmark transcripts

items.content_text: On 15 October 2026, the European Commission launched the RAISE AI in Science Enablers initiative for voluntary private and philanthropic support to European research. The Commission names seven initial participants and describes access to models, computing, software, data and training. Its pledge portal gives selected terms: Frontiers lists more than €1.6 million in services, including curation for 1,000 Horizon Europe datasets and 100 data-publication grants, while Google pledges $3 million in cloud credits/tokens. The portal also describes other contributions, including research collaborations, model/API access and compute. These remain announced commitments; there is no total valuation, common access framework, delivery record or researcher-uptake measure. A separate Mistral AI–CERN physics-model partnership is announced without technical specifications.
items.title: European Commission launches RAISE in-kind pledging initiative for AI-enabled science

items.content_text: An arXiv preprint introduces GUI-SD-v2, which trains a mobile GUI agent in two stages: first to follow corrective privileged guidance, then to distill step-specific reasoning and task-relevant memory from its own interaction trajectories. With Qwen3-VL-Instruct-8B and Kimi-K3-generated supervision, the authors report 67.2%/79.3% Pass@1/Pass@3 on AndroidWorld and 25.6%/31.6% on the GUI-only MobileWorld subset, above the paper’s evaluated baselines under its settings. These are author-reported results on two mobile benchmark settings; code and data were stated as future releases, and neither independent reproduction nor broader transfer was established.
tags: Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences
items.title: GUI-SD-v2 reports higher mobile GUI-agent success after privilege-following and step-level memory distillation

items.content_text: An arXiv preprint models one published AI-control deployment route as access control, monitoring plus response, or visibility plus tracing plus containment. Under independent equal rare failures, its visible-component model has six size-three minimal cuts and failure probability asymptotic to 6ε³. Illustrative shared failure domains reduce the minimum underlying cut size to two or one, and a conditional derivation shows why stronger prevention can concentrate later recovery demands in harder failure regimes. The paper recommends explicit dependency mapping and recovery tests that preserve the initiating failure. These results are conditional analysis: the common-cause examples are not claims about Google DeepMind’s implementation, and no operational probabilities are calibrated.
items.title: A conditional reliability model shows how shared failures erase nominal AI-control redundancy

items.content_text: EnSIMem stores dialogue-grounded entity/property indexes as addresses into theme-coherent episodes, then decomposes a query into evidence requirements and retrieves the original source turns needed to answer it. The authors report LoCoMo overall accuracy of 90.6% under GPT-4o-mini and 90.0% under Qwen3-32B, and LongMemEval accuracy of 92.8% under both evaluators. A fixed LoCoMo ablation reports 96.59% for structured entity/type/property retrieval versus 86.36% for dense retrieval. These are paper-reported, LLM-evaluated results. The reported online latency is 14.4 seconds versus 5.70 seconds for MEMORA(P); some comparator rows are transcribed rather than rerun.
items.title: EnSIMem links structured memory indexes to source-grounded conversational evidence

items.content_text: The paper analyzes sampled-token on-policy distillation (OPD) and defines an information-efficiency ratio (IER) for the reliability of reverse-KL gradient estimates at a fixed prefix. It approximates IER on a finite top-K candidate set and combines the resulting token ranking with existing usefulness scores. Across selected mathematical and medical reasoning settings, the authors report that combined selectors can approach or exceed full OPD at 0.1%–1% token budgets, with mixed results across settings. This concerns token selection for the loss: full student responses and teacher supervision remain computed, and proportional end-to-end compute savings are not established.
items.title: IER adds gradient-estimation reliability to sparse on-policy distillation

items.content_text: The Oct 15 arXiv paper introduces MLExpert, a 35B-total/approximately 3B-active MoE initialized from Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and post-trained for long-horizon machine-learning engineering using hierarchical agentic SFT and Windowed Interaction RL. On a 22-task MLE-Bench Lite subset, the authors report 72.7% any-medal versus 37.9% for the base under their unified harness; under Claude Code they report 69.7% versus 42.4%. A 10-task NatureBench Lite comparison also reports gains over the base. These are paper-reported benchmark results, not an independent demonstration of autonomous AI research or recursive self-improvement.
items.title: MLExpert reports post-training gains on long-horizon machine-learning engineering

items.content_text: RoboFollow is an author-designed benchmark intended to test whether embodied policies use language to select a task when the visual scene supports multiple valid actions. Across four controlled scene families, nine evaluated VLA/WAM policies and L0–L3 visual or semantic perturbations, the paper reports sharp declines in selected policies’ Intent Scores—for example, pi0 falls from 98.2% to 0.0% on a Scene 1 layout change, and pi0.5 falls from 100.0% to 34.2% on a Scene 2 combined perturbation. A small pi0.5 robot pilot reports 20/40 successes on training instructions versus 6/40 on a different held-out instruction set, but the comparison is unmatched. These paper-reported results diagnose sensitivity in this short-horizon controlled benchmark; they do not establish general deployment failure rates or broad embodied-agent unreliability.
items.title: A controlled robot benchmark reports instruction-grounding declines under scene changes

items.content_text: A paper trains a 7B concept generator with reinforcement learning to propose reasoning strategies for a frozen larger answer model. On a 1,000-item DeepMath hard subset selected for zero Qwen2.5-32B success in 128 prior rollouts, the authors report pass@128 of 39.2% versus 19.0% for repeated sampling at the same answer-rollout allocation; on a similarly filtered Omni-MATH 2 set, they report 18.60% versus 11.29%. A limited transfer evaluation reports a smaller gain when steering Llama-3.3-70B. These remain author-reported, task-filtered benchmark results: evaluation reuses the Qwen answer model as judge, training reward estimation is compute-heavy, and no independent reproduction or broad cost advantage is established.
items.title: A trained concept generator raises reported pass@128 on filtered hard-math sets

items.content_text: An arXiv paper proposes a governed benchmark for agents delivering post-trained models, where stage-level decisions are scored from platform-recorded evidence and a held-out acceptance gate checks the delivered model. Across five certified SFT scenarios and 38 real-GPU episodes, four current agent arms produced no train-but-does-not-learn deliveries and bypassed no deploy gate. Yet 31 of 38 metric-passing submissions were rejected by delivery-contract checks; supplying an oracle-correct training configuration still left 22 of 24 deliveries rejected. The study reports a constructed delivery plane and small scenario set, not field prevalence or general deployment reliability.
items.title: A post-training delivery benchmark separates model gains from successful service delivery

items.content_text: An arXiv paper introduces HALTER, a system for scoring and resetting real-robot long-horizon manipulation trials. On one Franka Panda arm, the authors report successful resets in 76% of 100 episodes across four tasks, compared with 52% for AutoEval and 65% for a motion-planning baseline; reset-verification accuracy is 91%, and operator time is 24 versus 88 minutes for manual resets. On three held-out tasks, HALTER reportedly resets 74.7% of episodes versus 1.3% for per-task reset. Results are author-reported, limited to one robot and seven tabletop tasks; one main task favors the motion-planning baseline.
items.title: HALTER reports autonomous resets for long-horizon robot evaluations

items.content_text: An arXiv preprint analyzes 259 papers reporting agentic-security attack success rates from a query-retrieved English-language arXiv corpus. The authors report that 58.0% of a seeded hand-coded sample of 50 papers (95% Wilson CI 44.2–70.6) reported neither a variance estimate nor repeated runs; revised automated detectors estimate 65.3% across all 259. They identify six choices that can change what an ASR measures, including evaluation unit, success oracle, attacker adaptivity, and defense knowledge. The paper argues these differences can make cross-paper values incomparable. It does not claim any individual paper is wrong, and its ranking-reversal estimates are analytical rather than observed defense comparisons.
items.title: Agent-security attack success rates lack a shared measurement contract

items.content_text: A September 2026 paper proposes Flash-Cache, which fuses KV-cache operations, and Flash-Verify, which lets a diffusion LLM draft and verify candidate tokens without an auxiliary model. On one NVIDIA A100 80GB running LLaDA-1.5, the authors report 5.1× speedup over Elastic-Cache on GSM8K at 512 tokens and 11.0× on HumanEval at 512 tokens. Across the paper’s 512-token settings, reported throughput reaches 210.6 tokens/s on GSM8K, 210.1 on MATH, 185.6 on HumanEval and 148.2 on MBPP; accuracy varies by task, and the fastest setting is not always the most accurate. The authors provide an Apache-2.0 repository with benchmark scripts, but no code was run; its README flags a possible difference between paper and adapter descriptions of the verification threshold. These remain author-reported results from one model and hardware setup.
tags: Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
items.title: Flash-dLLM reports faster diffusion-model decoding with fused KV caching and self-verification

items.content_text: A September 2026 TMLR paper reports that BF16 versus FP16 inference produced different greedy-decoding sequences on 49–100% of prompts across six tested models and three benchmarks. The authors report that recomputing only the language-model output head in FP32 when the top-two logit margin is small improved exact agreement by 22–36 percentage points on an A10G and 12–21 points on L4/A100 GPUs, with under 4% latency overhead at batch sizes up to 4. They report that the intervention’s benefit disappears at batch size 8 or higher and under end-to-end FP8. These are author-reported results, not an independent reproduction.
items.title: A study finds BF16 and FP16 can produce different greedy LLM outputs

items.content_text: A September 29 preprint introduces Uni-LaDiR, which encodes multimodal teacher reasoning steps in shared latent tokens and generates them with a diffusion reasoner. The authors report a 7.3% relative mean gain over ILVR across four mathematical and logical visual benchmarks and a 6.1% relative success gain over LaST0 across ten simulated RLBench tasks. Results remain author-reported; the manipulation evaluation is simulated, and broader VLM comparisons use methods with different training recipes.
items.title: Uni-LaDiR reports shared latent reasoning gains on visual reasoning and simulated manipulation benchmarks

items.content_text: A September 23 preprint describes OmniFysics-Nano-V2, a 4B-parameter omni-modal model trained with explicit physical supervision for image, video, audio, speech and text. The authors report results on named physical-understanding benchmarks that exceed the listed Qwen2.5-Omni-7B comparison scores on those tests. The paper reports mixed results across general multimodal benchmarks, and the embodied evaluation is simulator/engine-in-the-loop rather than physical robot deployment. No independent reproduction was performed.
items.title: OmniFysics-Nano-V2 reports gains on physical-understanding benchmarks

items.content_text: The September 21 preprint introduces MIGU, which fuses a VLM-derived semantic prior with a 3D pointing likelihood and can choose between proceeding and asking a binary clarification question. On a 100-scenario instruction-grounding benchmark, the authors report 83% object-level accuracy, beating the tested baselines. In a separate real-world mobile-manipulation study, eight tasks were repeated three times: planning success is reported at 83.3% with semantic-geometric fusion, versus 45.8% for semantic-only and 41.7% for geometry-only grounding; adding clarification raises the fused condition to 91.7%. The results are paper-reported. The study does not supply independent reproduction, broad task coverage or evidence of reliability in deployment.
items.title: MIGU reports improved pointing-and-language grounding and clarification gains on a mobile-manipulation robot

items.content_text: An Oct 15 arXiv preprint reports that four Gemini 4 Argon coding agents completed Minecraft’s main survival objective by defeating the Ender Dragon in one randomly generated Java Edition 1.20.4 world on Easy difficulty. The agents coordinated through in-game chat and shared memory, wrote 2,783 programs, and reached the win 27 hours 14 minutes after the first program; the paper says no human intervened. The authors report that the server log recorded the final advancement, and describe 605 deaths and six server restarts. This is a single author-reported run, not a reliability result. Mineflayer exposed nearby world state, including information unavailable to a human player, and supplied pathfinding; prior knowledge of Minecraft was not removed.
items.title: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents complete Minecraft’s main survival objective in one 27-hour run

items.content_text: The September 22 preprint introduces Taste-Bench, 502 decision-fork questions mined from software-engineering and AI-research agent trajectories. Models choose between two directions before seeing later outcomes; a question counts correct only when the choice is correct in both candidate orders, making chance accuracy 25%. The authors report GPT-5.6 Sol at 59.7% average accuracy, falling to 21.0% across models when decisive evidence appears only after substantial later work. On held-out engineering questions from unseen tasks, a distilled Qwen3.6-27B student scores 47.9% versus 30.0% for its base model. In a separate 41-task SWE-bench Pro experiment, a fixed executor succeeds on 14.6% with no advice and 33.7% with student advice; correct advice reaches 39.0%. These author-reported findings are not independent reproductions.
items.title: Taste-Bench measures long-horizon decision choices and reports gains from distillation

items.content_text: The 2026-09-22 preprint compares how an LLM agent handles assigned-work state when it is left in the transcript, displayed as a checklist, turned into per-turn directives or enforced by a gate that rejects state-violating actions. The authors report that receipt-backed directives and enforcement raise strict task-lifecycle success in controlled episodes, with gains varying by model and reasoning regime. In one tau-squared-bench airline case, enforcement raises Qwen3-235B pass at one from 0.39 to 0.54; on PM-Bench, showing the record can match or outperform gates, while matcher-based enforcement hurts a smaller model on semantic cue tasks. These are author-reported, bounded results: enforcement depends on correct compiled state and request matching, and the study does not establish general deployed-agent reliability.
items.title: Receipt-backed task state improves agent workflow reliability in bounded tests, with matcher-dependent failures

items.content_text: A Chinese-language notice dated October 12 and published by the Cyberspace Administration of China on October 15 announces a two-month, multi-agency campaign against improper marketing and sensationalized military-related content online. The ten listed categories include AI-generated fake military dramas, stories and videos. The notice directs authorities to require platform review and cleanup, but reports no implementation results, AI-specific technical requirements or measured effects.
tags: Ministry of Veterans Affairs of the People's Republic of China
Central Military Commission Political Work Department
Central Military Commission Political and Legal Affairs Commission
items.title: China's CAC announces a two-month campaign against misleading military content, including AI-generated fabrications

items.content_text: On September 22, 2026, Palo Alto Networks announced Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense as a worldwide annual-subscription service. The company describes a full-estate baseline scan followed by recurring testing as customer environments change, using a proprietary harness that routes work among gated frontier and open-weight models, threat intelligence and offensive-security staff. It says the service validates attack paths across applications, APIs, cloud infrastructure, repositories and network assets, then prioritizes remediation. The release reports customer findings but supplies no assessment denominator, independent validation or measured remediation outcome; the announcement supports product availability and described design, not service efficacy.
items.title: Palo Alto announces continuous frontier-model offensive security service with unverified efficacy

items.content_text: A September 21, 2026 Hugging Face community article and the public relore repository describe a tool that indexes issue and pull-request history with author and trust metadata, then joins that history to current-code search in a maintained clone. Its project-authored, model-judged retrieval evaluation reports Recall@10 rising from 0.938 to 1.000 for 48 Transformers failure queries after query expansion, and from 0.375 to 0.475 for 40 precedent queries. The larger pooled rationale result is contaminated by same-thread answer leakage; the leak-free rationale slices are only 7 and 9 examples. In one author-reported Transformers case, relore found two existing fix threads and the agent avoided writing another patch; a code-browsing overview reportedly used about 5% of the tokens needed to read a whole file. These results support bounded accounts of retrieval and one field case, not a general reduction in duplicate work, better patches or higher coding-agent productivity.
items.title: Relore combines repository decision history with current-code search; reported retrieval gains remain narrow

items.content_text: An October 15 preprint introduces MindEval2, pairing psychologist-developed operational rubrics with MindSim, a longitudinal synthetic-patient simulator with cross-session memory. The authors evaluate 18 language models and report that guidance calibration—over-exploring, under-guiding or giving poorly matched advice—accounts for 60–88% of each model’s rubric findings; under-guiding rises from 12% of early replies to about 70% from turn 9 onward. The evaluation uses 50 synthetic patient profiles and a single GPT-6.1 Sol judge. It is a benchmark result, not evidence of clinical effectiveness or safety in patient care.
items.title: MindEval2 reports guidance-calibration failures across mental-health support models

items.content_text: A September 20 preprint introduces pseudo self-distillation (PSD), which uses outputs from a closed-model oracle as prompt context for a Qwen model acting as a privileged teacher, then trains a student to match its output distribution without access to teacher logits or hidden states. In the authors’ LoCoMo test, a PSD-trained Qwen3-4B receives an overall LLM-judge score of 0.8699 versus 0.849 for the original MEMORA pipeline using GPT-4.1-mini; the paper also reports improvements over its own SFT checkpoint at all three tested Qwen sizes. These are author-reported results. The reported score comparison does not establish total training-plus-inference cost savings.
items.title: PSD reports transferring black-box memory construction into small Qwen models

items.content_text: A September 19 preprint introduces FireWorldBench, a multimodal benchmark for reasoning about fire dynamics across temperature, visibility, smoke, flow, combustion and ventilation. It contains 520 fire-world entries—494 controlled simulations and 26 real-world-aligned event groups—with 9,074 question-answer items. The authors evaluate text-only structured observations and rendered physical-field visualizations; they report that leading models remain substantially less accurate on visual evidence and higher-order causal/intervention tasks than on simpler physical-perception tasks. These results are author-reported and the real-world-aligned component is limited to 26 event groups.
tags: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology
items.title: FireWorldBench tests multimodal models on coupled-field fire dynamics

items.content_text: An October 13 arXiv revision presents EGMemory, a training-free memory framework that preserves message provenance and state histories in evidence chains, verifies proposed updates against source messages and prior state, and navigates evidence iteratively at answer time. The authors report 68.2% accuracy on GroupMemBench and 77.9% on EverMemBench, 22.7 and 21.4 percentage points above the strongest evaluated baselines; on dyadic LoCoMo they report 73.6%, 4.3 points above the best listed baseline. The results are paper-reported and have not been independently reproduced.
items.title: EGMemory reports evidence-chain memory gains on multi-actor conversation benchmarks

items.content_text: Reuters reports that Meta tested human contractors quietly handling some calls placed by its Muse agent, based on internal company posts reviewed by the news agency. The report says a Meta vice president acknowledged missing disclosures and said the feature had been rolled back for now; Meta’s spokesperson described the test as gathering feedback and said the calling feature would launch only with proper disclosure. The internal posts and underlying test were not independently inspected by the research desk.
items.title: Reuters reports Meta paused a human-call fallback test in its Muse agent after disclosure concerns

items.content_text: The Brazilian National Laboratory for Scientific Computing (LNCC), a research unit of MCTI, reports that it is leading technical studies for a new AI-focused high-performance computer planned for Macaíba, Rio Grande do Norte, as part of the Brazilian AI Plan. The FACC official register lists Public Selection No. 27/2026 as an in-person procurement published on 20 August 2026 and closing on 4 November 2026, seeking integrated HPC for AI, research, technological development and innovation. LNCC’s report states a procurement value of R$ 959,040,959.04 and says the system is intended for model development, training and inference and to serve public agencies, researchers, universities and Brazil’s AI innovation ecosystem. The notice, terms and linked attachments did not load in this review. The available sources establish the planned procurement, not an award, delivered configuration, operational compute or measured performance.
tags: Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação
Fundação de Apoio ao Desenvolvimento da Computação Científica
items.title: Brazil opens a public selection for a national AI supercomputer led by LNCC

items.content_text: An arXiv preprint presents SCOPE, a post-training recipe for computer-use agents that combines capability demonstrations, safe continuations around environmental hazards, explicit refusals and subsequent capability RL. On Qwen3.5-9B, the authors report 54.17% OSWorld task success and 64.30% OS-BLIND attack avoidance after RL, with a 58.80% harmonic mean in their benchmark setting. Matched-step ablations suggest refusal trajectories contribute most of the measured attack-avoidance gain, while safe-continuation trajectories better preserve task utility. These are author-reported results on one model and benchmark suite; OS-BLIND does not distinguish safe continuation from refusal or incidental task failure, and the aggregate is not a deployment safety guarantee.
items.title: SCOPE reports joint capability and safety post-training for computer-use agents

items.content_text: An arXiv preprint introduces Distributional Adversarial Recurrent Training (DART), which trains recurrent reasoning models with a locally perturbed target distribution and an input-conditioned adversarial critic. The authors report improved easy-to-hard results for Deep Thinking Systems on mazes and chess puzzles and for Tiny Recursive Models on masked Sudoku. For 31×31 mazes, reported accuracy is 99.91±0.13% with DART versus 73.92±26.01% with cross-entropy; at 50% Sudoku masking and depth 56, reported accuracy is 38.0±0.1% versus 32.4±1.7%. Chess still shows late-iteration degradation with DART alone; combining it with progressive training is reported to improve final accuracy. These are paper-reported results, not independently reproduced here.
tags: VNU – University of Engineering and Technology
items.title: DART reports improved easy-to-hard accuracy for recurrent reasoning models

items.content_text: An arXiv preprint introduces ACLArena, a controlled study of capability retention across multi-stage agent post-training. On Qwen3-8B-Base, the authors report that sequential math, search, e-commerce and instruction-following stages can overwrite earlier capabilities: after e-commerce training, AIME26 fell from 23.33 to 6.04 and Natural Questions from 45.2 to 14.6. They compare multi-teacher on-policy distillation, replay-based supervised fine-tuning and model merging, then propose Mixture of Low-Rank Experts (MLE), which combines replay-trained shared behavior with separate RL-trained LoRA experts routed by environment context. Reported results approach task-specific experts on several tasks, but the fixed curriculum, single model family and observable-context routing leave transfer and deployment costs unresolved.
items.title: ACLArena reports task forgetting in sequential agent training and tests routed LoRA experts

items.content_text: An arXiv preprint reports X-AuT, a progressive pruning and cross-scale recovery recipe for the Qwen3-ASR-0.6B audio encoder. Across ten public Chinese-English ASR benchmarks, the authors report that 18-to-16-layer compression lowered unweighted macro error from 5.61% to 5.27%; a 14-layer model used 20.7% fewer audio-tower parameters with 5.75% macro error. For that 14-layer model, the reported encoder latency fell 21.4% on an in-vehicle PPU and 11.4% on an H800, but end-to-end latency fell only 4.7% and 2.6%. These are single-run, author-reported results on one model family; no repeated-seed uncertainty or independent reproduction is reported.
items.title: X-AuT reports progressive Qwen3-ASR encoder compression with modest end-to-end latency gains

items.content_text: The authors of arXiv:2609.22512 report correlated errors across open-weight and frontier LLM judges. In their main ten-judge open-weight bank, average pairwise error correlation is 0.206 and the variance-based effective ensemble size is 3.51 on 1,133 RewardBench preference pairs; this is not a claim about majority-vote accuracy. In resampled 100-pair Focus panels, a pooled-vote significance test disagrees with an item-level test in 28% of panels. Three cross-provider frontier judges show error correlation of 0.56 on RewardBench, based on a small bank and relatively few residual errors. The authors find that different error structures favor different filters, while their tested dependence-aware filters do not outperform plain majority on the screened factuality and code settings. These are preprint results, not independently reproduced findings.
items.title: A preprint measures correlated errors across LLM judges and shows when consensus overstates evidence

items.content_text: Google DeepMind’s 15 October walkthrough describes a researcher-steered Antigravity/Gemini 3.8 Flash workflow that searches UniProt candidates, cross-checks sequence similarity, compares predicted structures and genomic context, and prepares a wet-lab protocol. The example names UniProt A0A0U0D591, a 97-amino-acid protein assigned to the Lactococcin 972 family; the company says the candidate and others are undergoing wet-lab validation. This is a first-party account of a computational candidate-selection workflow, not evidence of antibacterial efficacy or independent discovery performance.
items.title: Google DeepMind reports a human-steered Antigravity workflow for antimicrobial-peptide candidate search

items.content_text: Aolani’s September 21, 2026 announcement says it expects to deploy 22,000 NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra GPUs across two AI factories in Malaysia and the Philippines in early 2027. It says the collaboration brings its AI factory capacity above 100 MW and total deployment above 48,000 GPUs. These are forward-looking company statements: this review did not verify financing, construction, permits, delivery, operational capacity, utilization, or NVIDIA’s corroboration.
items.title: Aolani announces plans for 22,000 Blackwell Ultra GPUs across Malaysia and the Philippines

items.content_text: PrismML’s September 17, 2026 whitepaper reports Ternary Bonsai 2 27B at 52.8 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 60.8% resolved on SWE-bench Verified, compared with 69.7 and 80.6 for Qwen3.8-27B FP16. The paper says the Terminal-Bench run used Terminus-2 on 89 tasks with one attempt each, while SWE-bench Verified used mini-swe-agent on all 500 instances. These two agentic results are separate from the paper’s 20-benchmark aggregate, where Bonsai 2 scores 83.9 versus 85.4 (98.2% retention). This is a bounded vendor-reported quality tradeoff, not independent validation; checkpoint hashes, run traces and independent reproduction remain open.
items.title: Bonsai 2 27B whitepaper reports roughly three-quarter retention on two agentic coding benchmarks

items.content_text: A September 14, 2026 arXiv paper introduces Fixed-SAE Track: it trains one shared sparse autoencoder per analyzed layer on activations pooled across a base model and its RL checkpoints, then freezes the feature directions to track representation shifts. In the main Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct math-RL setting, the authors report gradual late-layer drift concentrated in formatting and reasoning scaffolds. Steering amplified features at dose α=10 raises strict accuracy from 0.050 to 0.192, close to the short-RL final model’s 0.175, while lenient reasoning accuracy changes more modestly. The paper also reports that all 29 selected GSM8K problems that shift from greedy-base-wrong to RL-right are solved by base sampling at k=64; however, 2000 additional RL steps raise lenient accuracy from 0.300 to 0.408, and directly injecting a necessary reasoning feature set recovers little. The approximately 80% headline therefore concerns a bounded short-RL extractability/format effect, not a general claim that RL only elicits existing capability. Results are author-reported and not independently reproduced.
tags: The Chinese University of Hong Kong
items.title: Fixed-SAE Track traces bounded, format-heavy RL shifts in a small reasoning model

items.content_text: A September 21, 2026 arXiv paper introduces H-Spec, a parallel speculative-decoding drafter that combines Mamba state initialized from the target model’s last-position hidden state with attention that reuses the target KV cache in place. This removes a separate drafter-side KV cache. Under the authors’ matched training recipe, H-Spec reports 5.0–13.3% higher mean accepted length and 5.3–12.6% higher batch-size-1 inter-token-latency speedup than the best baseline across three targets and eight tasks, with paired bootstrap 95% intervals above zero. On one NVIDIA A100 80G using vLLM, the paper reports higher throughput and lower KV-cache utilization across concurrency 8–128. These remain author-reported results; the paper notes slower drafting below concurrency 32 and initially on shorter inputs, and requires matching drafter and target K/V dimensions. Independent serving reproduction and transfer beyond the measured setup remain open.
items.title: H-Spec removes the separate drafter KV cache in parallel speculative decoding

items.content_text: A September 21, 2026 arXiv paper introduces InfoPPO, which measures temporal progression in RLVR by accumulated information density rather than raw token count and uses that density to adapt policy clipping. In author-reported Mean@16 results across five competition-style mathematics benchmarks, average accuracy for Qwen3-4B/8B/14B is 34.9/41.2/49.4, compared with DAPO at 32.2/36.3/45.3. The paper reports response lengths broadly comparable to DAPO/DAPO-FT and shorter than PPO in its table, and adds one Llama-3.2-3B appendix comparison. These are CLAIMED paper results, not independently reproduced; no seed-level uncertainty is reported in the main aggregate table, and task/model transfer remains open.
tags: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
items.title: InfoPPO uses information-time discounting and adaptive clipping for long-horizon language-model RL

items.content_text: Li Auto’s ME-Brain technical report describes an embodied system combining an external multimodal memory, a cognitive module and an action model, and reports comparisons on RoboMME, RoboDojo and six physical manipulation tasks. These are author-reported results: the real-robot evaluation used a Piper dual-arm platform and 10 trials per task. No independent reproduction, released artifact or broad deployment result is established here.
items.title: ME-Brain reports memory-guided improvement across simulated and small-scale robot tasks

items.content_text: Beijing opened a call for proposals to build domain scientific data centers for AI-enabled research. The notice and its construction requirements specify data aggregation and governance, AI-Ready preprocessing and annotation pipelines, multimodal processing, research-trajectory datasets, audited access controls, and connection to the municipal open-science-data platform with API and integrated-compute services. Projects may last up to three years; company applicants must provide matching funds at a minimum 2:1 ratio to municipal science funding. Applications are due October 28, 2026. The call establishes requirements, not awards, operating centers or delivered research-data access.
tags: Beijing Municipal Science and Technology Commission
items.title: Beijing opens a call for scientific data centers to support AI-enabled research

items.content_text: Participating EU member states adopted Ireland’s Dublin Declaration on 14 October 2026. The document records shared intentions across AI safety and resilience, trusted adoption, European sovereignty, infrastructure and skills, sustainability, public-sector procurement, and international cooperation. It is a political commitment, not a binding legal instrument; this record does not establish new legal duties, funded delivery or implementation.
items.title: EU member states set shared priorities for safe, sovereign and sustainable AI in the Dublin Declaration

items.content_text: A September 21 preprint introduces EvoPathBench, an author-built benchmark for tracking persistent agent memory and skill updates across 1,800 ordered task streams. It tests held-out generalization, retention after unrelated learning and adaptation after a rule changes. In the reported experiments, gains often weakened under distribution shift, retention loss was concentrated in some paths, and no method showed reliable rule adaptation; adaptation effects were not statistically significant after Holm correction. The paper also reports that update-selection safeguards reduce harmful accepted changes but miss more beneficial ones. These results come from fixed configurations in constructed trading environments combining public Binance data and calibrated synthetic trajectories. They are not independently reproduced and do not establish deployed-agent or real-market performance.
items.title: EvoPathBench tests whether self-evolving agents retain and adapt capabilities

items.content_text: A September 21 preprint introduces TAME, which combines evolving prompt feedback with a targeted sparse-autoencoder activation penalty during reinforcement learning to improve the monitorability of VLM chain-of-thought. In experiments on Qwen3-VL-8B and Gemma-3-12B-it across GQA, VIRL-39k and SPA-VL, the authors report that monitorability can decline while task reward rises, and that targeted feature interventions and TAME partly restore their operational monitorability measure. A blinded paired human evaluation favors TAME on monitorability by 12.50 percentage points on VIRL and 13.75 on SPA-VL; two held-out monitor families also report positive changes on the same frozen traces. Task accuracy and general-capability effects are small or mixed and vary by setting. These are author-reported results; the operational metric does not establish faithful access to internal reasoning or better real-world safety.
items.title: TAME reports improved VLM chain-of-thought monitorability with mixed capability trade-offs

items.content_text: A September 17 preprint proposes Causal Latent Revision (CaLR), a method for diffusion language models that uses a teacher model to extract concept-level dependencies and then guides latent updates with a causal topology matrix and implicit differentiation. The authors evaluate a LoRA-tuned LLaDA-8B on several reasoning and coding tasks. The paper's numerical account is internally difficult to reconcile: §4.2 reports GSM8K accuracy of 58.36%, while Table 1's flattened header and CaLR-8B values leave the corresponding task column ambiguous. This review records the proposed method but does not rely on disputed performance magnitudes; results remain author-reported and unreproduced.
tags: China Telecom Institute of Artificial Intelligence
items.title: CaLR proposes causal-topology-guided latent revision for diffusion reasoning

items.content_text: On October 15, the Financial Stability Board published a final report with 12 nonbinding practices for responsible AI adoption by financial institutions. The practices span board-level oversight and organization-wide risk governance, plus lifecycle controls for use-case assessment, model selection, data, transparency, performance, human oversight, cyber/ICT and third-party dependencies. The FSB says the report was revised after public consultation, including broader documentation and third-party-risk treatment and additional discussion of agentic and multi-agent systems. It calls the practices an adaptable toolkit rather than a binding standard; the report says agentic-specific guidance remains nascent.
items.title: FSB issues 12 nonbinding AI governance practices for financial institutions

items.content_text: OpenAI's October 15 GPT-Live-1.1 system card reports mixed voice-safety evaluation results. On its voice-native production-prompt set, the company reports no statistically significant regressions versus GPT-Live-1. On its deliberately difficult synthetic-prompt set, it reports statistically significant regressions for GPT-Live-1.1 in sexual, mental-health, emotional-reliance and gore categories; it also reports slight regression on a restrictions-respect evaluation and mixed changes on blocker-disclosure and broken-search tasks. These are first-party results, and neither prompt set estimates safety-event prevalence in production traffic.
items.title: GPT-Live-1.1 system card reports voice-safety regressions on synthetic adversarial prompts

items.content_text: On October 15, 2026, Anthropic reported that it had onboarded six METR employees with company hardware, office space and access to internal tools and systems roughly comparable to those used by its risk-assessment teams. Anthropic says METR may publish analyses of its risk levels, incidents and practices; Anthropic cannot veto publication but may require redactions within narrow predefined categories, and METR may characterize those redactions publicly. The team is siloed from other METR work. This is a first-party report of an operating access arrangement, not independent confirmation of practical access or evaluator independence. The post reports no completed evaluation findings or safety outcome.
items.title: Anthropic reports six METR evaluators onboarded with employee-like access and publication rights

items.content_text: A September 21, 2026 Cognizant AI Lab post and linked public repository describe a 75-million-parameter autoregressive transformer trained from scratch for ARC-AGI. Cognizant reports about 76% pass@2 on the public ARC-AGI-1 evaluation set after a little over four hours of training and evaluation on one NVIDIA H100; an eight-model ensemble reportedly reaches about 80%. The post also reports about 17% on ARC-AGI-2 for one model and about 22% for the ensemble, while a faster approximately 17-minute configuration reaches about 44% on ARC-AGI-1. The repository says headline scores average multiple seeds, but its example pages show best-seed results among eight. These are first-party reported results on public evaluation tasks, not a private leaderboard result or an independent reproduction. The linked code and evaluation recipe were inspected at the README level but not executed or audited.
items.title: Cognizant reports a 75M transformer reached about 76% pass@2 on ARC-AGI-1 public evaluation tasks

items.content_text: A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint introduces expected-accepted-length (EAL) training for greedy verification and window-total-variation (WTV) training for sampling-based speculative decoding. Across author-run Qwen3 and Gemma4 configurations and five benchmarks, the authors report higher mean acceptance lengths for matched objectives, with larger gains under sampling than greedy verification. In Qwen3-8B/Qwen3-0.6B tree decoding, WTV raises reported mean acceptance length from 4.998 to 5.750 at temperature 1.0 and from 4.304 to 4.780 at 0.5; under greedy verification, KL+EAL changes 4.494 to 4.503 while WTV alone is weaker at 4.428. The paper measures acceptance length, not end-to-end latency or serving cost. These results are claimed by the preprint authors and have not been independently reproduced.
items.title: Acceptance-aware training improves reported speculative-decoding acceptance length in matched regimes

items.content_text: Aikido released Altar-1, a 328 GB W4A16/REAP-pruned derivative of GLM-5.3 intended for local defensive-security workloads. Aikido reports that pruning reduces its already-quantized parent from 488.2 GB to 328.0 GB while retaining 60.4% average recall per run, versus 61.5% for the parent, on an internal benchmark of 32 known vulnerabilities across 30 repositories with three runs per case. Both versions rediscovered the same 23 vulnerabilities at least once. The vendor says the model is configured for vLLM on four H200 GPUs. These are company-reported results from targeted known-CVE rediscovery inside a larger pipeline; they do not demonstrate blind vulnerability discovery, exploit validation, patch quality or independent performance.
items.title: Aikido reports a 328 GB pruned GLM-5.3 security model with near-parent CVE recall

items.content_text: The ZCode v3.15.1 repository commit dated 2026-10-10 includes a Chinese NOTICE stating that its shared Agent execution adapter has no default operating-system sandbox, and that standalone CLI --prompt calls default to yolo when --mode is omitted. The pinned CLI source defines that fallback, and its permission service describes prompt-bypass rules and exceptions. These findings are scoped to the documented adapter and non-interactive CLI path; no packaged runtime was tested.
items.title: ZCode documents no default OS sandbox for its shared Agent adapter and a yolo default for non-interactive CLI prompts

items.content_text: A September 2026 preprint introduces JustMem, a long-term conversational-memory system that adapts retrieval breadth and source-reading fidelity to each query. In author-run tests using GPT-4.1-mini across LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S, it reports the best mean accuracy among the compared memory systems while using fewer generative-model tokens. Results are paper-reported and have not been independently reproduced.
items.title: JustMem reports adaptive long-term memory access with higher benchmark accuracy and lower model-token use

items.content_text: An October 14 preprint tests a simple reset rule for iterative agent research: after each round, discard every agent session and candidate history, then restart a communicating team from the best candidate and its score. Across four tasks in heuristic programming, kernel optimization and small-model training, four-agent teams with three resets reportedly improved mean best results by 10% over four parallel agents and 22% over one continuing agent, at the same total token cost. Each configuration used one model and was run three times per task. The authors attribute the gains to renewed exploration after sessions become anchored to prior attempts. These are author-reported benchmark results from a single agent/model harness, not an independent replication or evidence that forgetting is universally beneficial.
items.title: Agent research study reports a 10% average gain from periodically resetting search history

items.content_text: A September 18 work-in-progress preprint proposes RACER, which estimates an unseen expert’s query-level probability of being correct from a small context set using class-role relationships rather than absolute class identities. The authors prove a coherent class-relabelling invariance result, derive a Bayes-aligned deferral surrogate and provide a regret bound. In experiments, they report gains on synthetic expert benchmarks and budget-swept performance described as competitive or best on VinDr-CXR and CheXpert. On CheXpert, RACER-C and RACER-kernel report similar primary AURSBAC means (0.7243 and 0.7241 over 27 matched cells); the paper labels the comparisons descriptive and makes no significance claim. VinDr-CXR results use training annotations because official test labels lack radiologist identities; an out-of-distribution expert group is inferred from co-annotation patterns. Results remain author-reported and the code is not yet released.
items.title: RACER reports role-based competence estimates for routing to unseen human experts

items.content_text: A September 18 preprint introduces CogGym, a human-in-the-loop pipeline that standardizes cognitive-science experiments into a common format for matched human and language-model evaluation. The initial release reports 258 experiments from 100 papers across text, image and video, with 50 language models evaluated. On the paper’s reported human–model fit measure, the best models reach R² of 0.59 for text, 0.58 for image and 0.43 for video, below estimated human split-half references of 0.93, 0.95 and 0.92. A 15-experiment replication with 521 participants reports closer agreement between new and original human responses than between Gemini 3.1 Pro and the original responses. These are author-reported results; the 15-study check is a subset, not an independent reproduction of the full suite.
items.title: CogGym reports a large matched human–model evaluation suite with persistent behavioral gaps

items.content_text: A September 17 preprint compares shared-workspace teams with independent parallel agents on 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games. Using Claude Sonnet 4.6, the authors report full-game solve rates of 4.6% for teams of three and 8.0% for teams of five, versus 1.4% and 2.2% for the best of three and five independent attempts. Matching the reported team solve rates required 13 and 33 independent attempts, respectively. The paper also reports gains on two research-oriented tasks, but says communication can lose under limited compute or unclear feedback. These are author-reported results from one model and benchmark setup; the research desk did not reproduce them.
items.title: Authors report higher ARC-AGI-3 solve rates from test-time agent communication in a bounded setup

items.content_text: The Oct. 13 v2 of a paper on SURE-GRPO adds an 8B reasoning model to the earlier 4B-model account and reports a revised average abstention-performance gain of 14.7% while retaining answerable-task capability and reducing chain-of-thought length by 44%. The method rewards models for identifying missing information and avoiding redundant reasoning. The paper evaluates six model families and fine-tunes four models against accuracy-only and accuracy-plus-length-penalty baselines. These are author-reported results; training and evaluation were not independently reproduced.
items.title: SURE-GRPO reports more efficient abstention on underspecified reasoning tasks

items.content_text: A paper accepted at Interspeech 2026 describes three open small audio language models with 99M, 134M and 356M parameters, and an Android application for on-device inference. On the MMAU benchmark, the authors report that the 99M and 134M variants exceed the 167M Mellow model on the average scores shown; they also report 39–125 generated tokens per second on a Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra CPU using 15 audio-query pairs. Training code, checkpoints, mobile weights and Android application code are listed in the project repository. These are author-reported results; this review did not run the app or independently reproduce the benchmark or timing.
items.title: Samsone reports open 99M–356M audio models with Android CPU inference results

items.content_text: The Simons Foundation announced a joint $15 million effort with Anthropic and OpenAI to help mathematicians evaluate AI-assisted results and shape how the field uses AI. The foundation will manage awards, including an open call for workshops and related initiatives; the two labs will provide AI tools and computing resources to supported researchers, including in basic science. This establishes a funding and access program, not evidence that AI-generated mathematics has been validated or that the promised resources have been delivered.
items.title: Simons Foundation, Anthropic and OpenAI launch a $15M program for mathematics in the AI era

items.content_text: On 15 October 2026, Brazil’s data-protection authority (ANPD) published Technical Note 23/2026 analyzing consultation responses on platform regulation under the Marco Civil da Internet. The note says 74 submissions were received and 66 analyzed after screening; participation was led by private-sector contributors (47%), followed by organized civil society (30.3%). ANPD’s synthesis highlights calls for clearer platform-responsibility criteria, proportionate risk-based supervision, transparency reporting and complaint channels, and preventive safeguards against nonconsensual AI-generated intimate content. It also records disagreement over liability criteria, removal deadlines and the limits of agency authority. This is consultation analysis feeding ongoing regulation, not a final binding rule or a representative poll.
tags: Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD)
items.title: Brazil’s ANPD consultation analysis maps platform oversight and AI intimate-image proposals

items.content_text: A September 18 arXiv paper proposes Interrupt and Silent Modeling (ISM), which adds <interrupt> and <silent> decisions to an audio-language model so one watch-out intent can drive continuous alerts without a new query for every event. On ESC-50, the authors report 99.6% interrupt F1 and 100.0% recall for suppressing duplicate alerts. In a zero-shot Epic-Sounds evaluation, interrupt F1 was 67.5 and onset recall 96.7%, but irrelevant-silence recall was 10.1% and sustained-relevance recall 41.2%; duplicate suppression was not measured there. The reported 3.5-second mean latency comes from 400 constructed streams with the event onset fixed at five seconds. These are author-reported benchmark results, not evidence of wearable deployment or improved outcomes for Deaf and Hard of Hearing users.
items.title: AudioLLM interrupt-and-silent training reports proactive alerts in bounded sound benchmarks

items.content_text: A September 17 arXiv paper examines both how well language models generate GPU kernels and how much real workload time those kernels could affect. In its author-run tests on two A100-80GB GPUs, GPT-5.6 kernels passed correctness checks on 91.1% of 56 eligible KernelBench level-1 tasks, with 22 speedups surviving the paper's additional verifier. The authors' profiles put addressable work at 8.9–16.8% in their transformer workloads, implying roughly 1.3–2.5% end-to-end gains under their assumptions; one DLRM inference profile had 58.2% addressable time and an 8.63% projection. The paper also identifies four benchmark tasks where zero output passes the absolute-tolerance check and describes two author-run exploits. These results are author-reported and limited to one host, one GPU type, level-1 tasks and selected profiles; no independent reproduction was performed.
items.title: LLM-generated GPU-kernel gains depend on workload headroom and benchmark validity

items.content_text: An arXiv paper explicitly extends the authors’ NeurIPS 2025 Group Variance Policy Optimization (GVPO) work. Its new bounded contribution is a sequence-level formulation for on-policy distillation (OPD): the authors derive a GVPO loss for matching student and teacher distributions, then generalize it to positive response-weighted teacher/student distributions. The paper proves a consistency result for the transformed objective and shows how group-centering cancels partition-function terms, allowing sampling from the student or previous student policy without importance-sampling correction. The theory is author-reported; this activation did not audit proofs, experiments or code, and does not establish training gains in practice.
items.title: GVPO is extended to sequence-level on-policy distillation objectives

items.content_text: An arXiv paper introduces OpenMAS-GCom, a benchmark that compares multi-agent configurations with one component changed while tasks, models, prompts and budget limits are held fixed. The paper reports 17 configurations across 29 datasets in six domains, four interventions, and 400 frozen multi-document tasks requiring source-aware conflict resolution. In a five-dataset aggregate, it reports a 3.58 percentage-point mean score loss after specialist removal versus 0.58 points after critic removal. These are author-reported benchmark results; independent reproduction and broader task-weighted interpretation remain open.
items.title: OpenMAS-GCom reports controlled diagnosis of multi-agent system components

items.content_text: A September 2026 paper reports a temporal holdout study of partial evaluation for one production analytics agent: 574 runs of a 519-question benchmark were split evenly between calibration and held-out periods. It compares random sampling, historical caching, fixed subsets and adaptive testing. At 200 executed questions, the paper reports 1.37 percentage points of pass-rate mean absolute error in its results section, while its abstract reports 1.03 points for that budget. Difficulty-stratified fixed subsets were deployed for simplicity and tested on five additional agent families. These are author-reported results from one organization and task; the paper does not establish broad external reliability.
items.title: A production-agent study compares lower-cost recurring evaluation methods

items.content_text: In a Simplified Chinese issuer-distributed release dated September 21, Insilico Medicine announced a tens-of-millions USD agreement with an unnamed frontier foundation-model lab. The companies said they would combine the partner’s model architecture with Insilico’s MMAI Gym training framework and proprietary science data, conduct wet-lab validation, and pursue commercialization with revenue sharing. The announcement does not identify the counterparty or report a resulting model, measured biological outcome or realized revenue.
items.title: Insilico announces generative-biology model partnership with an unnamed frontier lab

items.content_text: A September 18 preprint proposes token-causal co-speech gesture generation using continuous motion latents and a flow-matching head, then distills only that head to one step while freezing the causal backbone. On BEAT2, the authors report a 3.08 FGD one-step student at 9.3 ms/token, compared with 3.17 at 24.4 ms/token for their eight-step teacher, and 0.246 real-time factor on a MacBook Air. These are author-reported results for a specialized avatar/embodied-agent benchmark; no independent reproduction or deployment transfer is established.
items.title: GestureFAR reports real-time continuous-latent streaming gestures on BEAT2

items.content_text: Peng Cheng Laboratory's Chinese report dated Sep 20, 2026 says its PEGA-SUS1 satellite entered its planned orbit after launch aboard a Lijian-1 Y18 rocket. The lab describes the satellite as integrating a 5G non-terrestrial-network base station and core network, onboard AI compute, laser communications and microwave communications into an orbital technology-validation platform. The report says in-orbit tests, including a planned 100 Gbps laser-communications experiment and multi-payload verification, would follow. It provides no measured on-orbit 5G, AI-compute or communications performance; the launch and payload configuration are lab-reported claims.
tags: Southern University of Science and Technology
items.title: Peng Cheng Laboratory reports PEGA-SUS1 launch with integrated satellite AI and 5G NTN payloads

items.content_text: Unbiased's September 17, 2026 product page describes Pareto 26.9 as a blended AI system that engages multiple frontier and open models in parallel and synthesizes their results for one response, rather than selecting a single model as a conventional router would. The provider publishes five benchmark scores for the release: DeepSWE 74, Terminal-Bench 4.0 51, MMMU-Pro 78, Humanity's Last Exam without tools 49, and ArXivMath 88. The provider states that it has not published measured task costs or a composite score for Pareto 26.9. The architecture and scores are provider-reported; they were not independently reproduced in this review.
items.title: Unbiased describes Pareto 26.9 as a blended multi-model inference system

items.content_text: The Sep 16, 2026 v2 of StarVLA-α studies a deliberately simple vision-language-action baseline built from a Qwen3-VL-4B backbone and an MLP action head. Across LIBERO, SimplerEnv, RoboTwin 2.0 and RoboCasa-GR1, the authors report competitive results for benchmark-specific policies and a single model jointly trained across datasets. On RoboChallenge, the paper reports 33.6% success and 54.5 progress for StarVLA-α on the ARX5 11-task set, versus 12.7% and 27.6 for π0.5. Additional appendices report real-world out-of-distribution tasks and LIBERO-Plus perturbation results. These measurements are paper-reported; independent reproduction, several physical-trial denominators and variability estimates remain open.
items.title: StarVLA-α reports competitive VLA results with a compact Qwen3-VL policy

items.content_text: In a September 13, 2026 report, Hacktron says three researchers used Claude Opus 4.8 and Opus 5 during a July security-research effort that chained a Discourse HEIF image-upload vulnerability with an OpenAI single-sign-on flaw. Hacktron reports that the chain reached employee ChatGPT/Codex accounts and that a human-directed Codex session opened a harmless pull request in an internal repository; it says testing stopped after the proof and OpenAI paid a bounty for the OpenAI-side finding. Discourse's July 28 security advisory independently confirms remote code execution through malformed HEIF uploads and credits Hacktron as reporter, but does not establish the OpenAI identity or account-access portion. The model's contribution and the reported impact remain first-party claims; skilled human guidance remained part of the work.
items.title: Hacktron reports model-assisted exploit chain reaching OpenAI employee accounts

items.content_text: Qwen released Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo on 9 October 2026 for text-to-image generation and image editing. Its official model card describes an accelerated checkpoint using the same 7B visual-generation architecture as Qwen-Image-2.1, a saved eight-step sampling schedule and prefix KV caching for reuse of text and reference-image context. Qwen also announced hosted Pro and Turbo APIs. The inspected materials report no matched latency, compute-cost or image-quality comparison; the step count alone does not establish a speed or efficiency gain.
items.title: Qwen releases Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo checkpoint with a saved 8-step schedule

items.content_text: Qwen announced Qwen-Image-2.1 on 20 September 2026 as an open-weight text-to-image and image-editing model with a 7B-parameter visual-generation component. Its official repository lists transparent RGBA generation, editing with up to 10 reference images, local masked/annotated edits and subject extraction among the supported features. The release is available through linked model repositories. The inspected release materials do not provide matched independent evidence for the claimed quality or efficiency improvements.
items.title: Qwen-Image-2.1 open-weight release adds RGBA and multi-reference image editing

items.content_text: A September 17 NYU Shanghai RITS report preserves a contemporaneous view of Xiaomi's public MiMo-V2.6 reinforcement-learning dashboard. It describes two runs, `mimo-v2.6-pro` and `mimo-v2.6-flash`, and reports that the dashboard showed about US$1.23 million cumulative spend, 27.6B and 35.2B processed tokens, long rollout contexts and intermediate DeepSWE scores. The page also showed run restarts associated with a VRAM issue and a dataset infrastructure error. These are dashboard values relayed by RITS, not independently audited telemetry. Xiaomi's dashboard currently renders only navigation labels, so current status and live values could not be checked.
items.title: NYU Shanghai report preserves a Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6 RL dashboard snapshot

items.content_text: Pieri et al. introduce PanoCaps, a human-annotated benchmark for full-scene captions with phrase-level pixel masks, and PANORAMA, which grounds each caption phrase by selecting from phrase-conditioned proposals generated by a pretrained segmenter. The authors report 3,470 images, 34.1K masks and 99.1% overall referenced-pixel coverage. They report strong results on PanoCaps and several related grounding tasks, including 75.5 overall gIoU on GroundingSuite versus 67.8 for the highest listed prior result. These are paper-reported evaluations; the research desk did not run the released code or model.
items.title: PANORAMA paper introduces dense phrase-to-pixel captioning and PanoCaps benchmark

items.content_text: Paul and Nandy's arXiv paper presents Governance-as-Code, a framework of 43 machine-checkable Rego acceptance criteria across six modules for selected EU AI Act obligations affecting generative systems. It makes operational thresholds and proxies explicit and emits Article-indexed audit evidence. In two author-reported case studies, the framework reproduced findings from manual expert audits; the authors report 12 findings reproduced across the cases and an 18-hour versus 72-hour chatbot audit. These results are paper-reported, not independently validated.
items.title: Governance-as-Code paper reports executable EU AI Act checks tested on two systems

items.content_text: A September 2026 preprint introduces BATON, which combines Bayesian Feedback Attribution within trajectories with equal-mass aggregation across trajectories. On Qwen2.5-Instruct models, the authors report gains over matched GRPO and GiGPO variants on ALFWorld, WebShop and seven-dataset search-augmented QA; a 2×2 ablation reports gains from each component separately. For example, ALFWorld success with Qwen2.5-1.5B rises from 72.9% to 85.6% for GRPO and from 86.8% to 94.1% for GiGPO. These are paper-reported results, not independently reproduced. The authors explicitly say the feedback likelihood measures model-based compatibility rather than causal effects of counterfactual actions.
tags: University of Science and Technology of China
items.title: BATON reports gains from balancing feedback attribution and trajectory mass in agent RL

items.content_text: A September 2026 preprint presents Cairn, a community reputation service where agents check a tool, data source or peer before use and add a rubric-based rating afterward. Its time-decayed Beta scorer shrinks uncertain ratings toward neutral. In simulations averaged over 100 seeds, reported scores tracked responder accuracy with mean absolute deviation 0.017, but pooled ratings failed sharply when dishonest raters approached or exceeded a majority. A live-corpus retrieval test reached R@5 0.65 overall and only 0.34 for mostly negative entities, so failure reports were harder to retrieve. A judge-rated sample of 5,000 active Moltbook agents produced scores uncorrelated with platform karma. These are paper-reported system and judge results; the paper does not establish improved downstream task outcomes, and Sybil attacks remain an open threat.
items.title: Cairn tests community reputation as shared memory for agent tools and services

items.content_text: A September 2026 preprint introduces KIR, a typed intermediate representation and compiler for agents authoring building information models in Revit. On a pinned KIR 0.8.1 snapshot, the author reports offline checks across 83 operation contracts, including typed refusals for 29 of 42 stress-test programs, 38 named absences among 377 witness obligations, and no vacuous certificate in 219 program-version runs. These are paper-reported results from project-authored artifacts; native Revit runs are separately reported from project records. The paper specifies but has not run a same-model, same-budget comparison against agents writing Revit code directly, and it demonstrates only Revit as an execution backend.
items.title: KIR reports typed checks for agent-authored building models, with direct-code comparison still open

items.content_text: The authors of SELF-INDEX describe an optimizer that diagnoses retrieval shortfalls, revises document keys, validates changes and uses simulated queries. Their paper reports improvements across BRIGHT with three retrievers, BrowseComp-Plus across four backbones and LongMemEval V2. For GPT-OSS-120B with BM25, reported BrowseComp-Plus accuracy rises from 31.08% to 58.92% while search calls decrease. LongMemEval results vary by task: several improve by 9.2–13.9%, while Gotchas is unchanged or lower. These are paper-reported results; independent replication and matched full optimization-cost comparisons remain open.
items.title: SELF-INDEX reports search and memory retrieval gains from revisable keys
